concepts.gloss_en: A righteous person / tzaddik (generic or collective; also used for the letter-symbol yud). Not necessarily the singular archetype.

members.note: representative; used generically and in plural (הצדיקים), e.g. 'צדיק הוא יוד', 'הצדיקים הם נקראים חכמי העדה'

concepts.gloss_en: THE Tzaddik — the singular archetype (tzaddik of the generation), the 'head'/master of the world from whom all generations are drawn.

members.note: definite archetype: 'נמשכין מן הצדיק שהוא הראש... הבעל־הבית של העולם'; 'הספד על סילוק הצדיק'

notes: Per Rule 2, the definite article plausibly shifts meaning: הצדיק in lm2:67/94 clearly denotes the singular archetype (the tzaddik of the generation as cosmic 'head'), while the bare צדיק form appears generically and in the plural/collective sense. Kept separate and flagged for human decision rather than merged. Note some proof quotes for the bare form contain vocalized 'הצדיק' inline, but the surface node form is צדיק.
